title: POC decision: compare usefulness and choose stop, iterate or MVP
description: Review the demonstrated POC with the owner before investing in the full implementation. Ask the owner to identify current work, its agent, the relevant discussion and whether intervention is needed; compare the same workflow in the existing Waystation dashboard. Record observed friction, context switching, loading/refresh behavior, integration effort, remaining host limits and whether the native view adds useful information or convenience. The outcome is an explicit owner choice: stop, make one bounded POC iteration, or define a small MVP with selected capabilities and acceptance. A negative result is useful evidence, not justification to continue the 19-task plan. Do not decide product value for the owner. If an earlier POC stage is blocked, present that finding immediately; only explicitly cancelled dependent tasks may be marked wont_do to let this review close without a successful demo. Completing or declining this task never automatically promotes full-plan work: only a separate affirmative owner decision may select tasks for an MVP.
acceptance: The review compares the native POC and existing dashboard using the same project/workflow and records the owner's ability to understand work, ownership and discussions.
An explicit owner decision and its reasons are recorded as stop, bounded iteration or a scoped MVP; no inferred approval from silence or mere technical success.
The 19 full-plan tasks remain unpromoted unless the owner explicitly chooses specific next work; an MVP decision does not automatically authorize the entire original plan.
Reusable POC code, limitations and any superseded deliverables are mapped to existing W tasks before further implementation, preventing duplicate Monitor, read-adapter or packaging work.
notes: Current milestone is the proof of concept in section 0 of docs/waystation-git-hermes-implementation-plan.md. This bounded experiment does not complete or authorize the full W04-W10 implementation. Preserve the user's native Hermes app preference. No agents are dispatched by task creation.
